storage_pet_loader_py.content:
import csv

from shelter_pet import ShelterPet
from foster_pet import FosterPet


def load_pets(path):
    pets = []

    with open(path, newline="") as file:
        for row in csv.DictReader(file):
            pet_class = FosterPet if row["foster"] == "yes" else ShelterPet
            pets.append(
                pet_class(
                    row["name"],
                    row["species"],
                    int(row["age"]),
                )
            )

    return pets

module-10-oop-quality-project-sketch0.title: Project story: make the shelter app safe for adoption weekend
module-10-oop-quality-project-sketch0.bodyMarkdown:
Harbor Street Animal Shelter is preparing for a busy adoption weekend. Its small Python intake app worked when the team handled only a few animals, but recent changes exposed several regressions: foster pets need specialized labels, collection reporting has started to spread across the runner, CSV intake can break on bad imports, and `mark_adopted()` can claim success without actually changing the pet's state.

The shelter does not need a rewrite. It needs confidence that the code it already depends on will keep working.

Your job is to **stabilize the application one failure at a time**, using tests to prove each repair.

The workspace grows with the problem:

```text
Milestone 1
main.py
models/
  shelter_pet.py
  foster_pet.py
tests/
  check_model.py

Milestone 2 adds
services/reporting.py
tests/check_reporting.py

Milestone 3 adds
storage/pet_loader.py
data/pets.csv
tests/check_loader.py

Milestone 4 adds
tests/check_adoption.py

Milestone 5 adds
tests/check_summary.py

Milestone 6 adds
tests/check_regression.py
README.md
```

By the end, the shelter has model, reporting, storage, state-transition, summary, and end-to-end regression coverage—and each file appears only when the project first needs it.
